paragraphs: Your team is working on development and integration of advanced language model capabilities. That is the kind of problem I have been working on. For my AstraZeneca-affiliated MSc dissertation I built an AI assistant that researchers could trust: it checks its answers against official databases, keeps working when those services go down, and is checked by about 65 automated tests. When the project switched AI providers, the same tests showed it still behaved, and I wrote up how often it got answers wrong so the team knew where it could be trusted.

At 180 Degrees Consulting I led the design in a five-person team that turned a startup's vague idea into a working AI prototype in three months, which the client's engineers then put into everyday use. The client's founder later called it "stable, production-ready" and said it arrived "ahead of schedule". At a hackathon I built a tool that answers in under 3 seconds for about £0.003 per question, and as a freelancer I built a private client an AI finance assistant that runs on his own server to keep costs down. Before my MSc, at Avasoft, I helped ship the first release of a money-management app for a company's 10,000+ employees.
The development and integration of advanced language model capabilities inspired me to focus on the company.
Could we spend 20 minutes on how the team builds retrieval-augmented generation systems with vector storage?

Found where the assistant went wrong with about 65 automated checks at three levels, fixed failures layer by layer, and reused the checks after changing AI provider (pytest).

projects.situation: Needed to know what fine-tuning can change in an 8B model on a free 15 GB GPU
bullets: Fine-tuned an 8-billion-parameter AI model on a free GPU, training only 0.52% of it, and raised correct maths answers from 16.2% to 27.3% on unseen problems (QLoRA, Llama).
Ran a data quality check on all 859,494 training examples, found 44,369 extra duplicates and hand-reviewed 181 suspect records before training (Python).
Reported the limits honestly: the gain came mostly from the model finishing its answers in time, not from better reasoning (50% vs 52% on finished answers).

projects.situation: Needed structure in unstructured airline support tickets
bullets: Built the text-cleaning and grouping steps for airline support tickets, and traced weak groupings (scores below 0.30) to repeated template wording (Python, scikit-learn).
Showed why airline support tickets would not group by topic (the wording was too similar) but could be sorted well with supervised models; our team project scored 79/100 (Python, scikit-learn).
In a five-person team, kept everyone's work on separate Git branches merged through reviewed pull requests, and ran the team's task board (Git, Trello).
